note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Maintenance of Registers
explain: Every company must maintain registers for its members, debenture holders, and other security holders.
Entries in the register must be made within 7 days of approval of allotment, transfer, or corporate action.
Companies with more than 50 members must maintain an index of names.
Foreign registers can be maintained outside India if authorized by the Articles of Association.
Companies can close their registers for up to 30 days at a time, maximum 45 days per year, after giving 7 days' notice.

flow.title: Process of Maintaining and Updating Registers
steps: Board approves allotment or transfer of securities
Make entries in register within 7 days
Update index if members exceed 50
File notice MGT-3 if maintaining foreign register
Give 7 days notice to close register

topics.example: ABC Ltd allotments 100 shares to Ramesh on 1st June. The company secretary must enter Ramesh's details in Form MGT-1 by 8th June.
remember: Form MGT-1 for Register of Members (Share capital).
Form MGT-2 for Debenture/Security holders.
7 days limit for making entries after Board approval.
Closure of register: Max 30 days at once, 45 days per year.
mistakes: Forgetting that index of members is compulsory only when members are 50 or more.
Assuming closure of register can exceed 30 days continuously without break.

quiz.q: Within how many days from Board approval must entries be made in the Register of Members?
quiz.why: Rule 5(1) requires entries to be made within 7 days of Board or Committee approval.

quiz.q: What is the maximum aggregate period for which a company can close its register of members in a year?
quiz.why: Section 91(1) permits closure for an aggregate maximum period of 45 days in each year, but not exceeding 30 days at any one time.

topics.title: Declaration of Beneficial Interest & Significant Beneficial Ownership
explain: If a registered shareholder does not hold beneficial interest, they must file a declaration in Form MGT-4 within 30 days.
The actual beneficial owner must file a declaration in Form MGT-5 within 30 days of acquiring interest.
The company must notify the Registrar of Companies in Form MGT-6 within 30 days of receiving MGT-4/MGT-5.
A Significant Beneficial Owner (SBO) holds at least 10% shares, voting rights, or dividend rights indirectly or with direct holdings.
An SBO must declare their status to the company in Form BEN-1 within 30 days of acquisition or change.

flow.title: Flow of Beneficial Interest Declarations
steps: Registered owner files Form MGT-4 in 30 days
Beneficial owner files Form MGT-5 in 30 days
Company files Form MGT-6 with ROC in 30 days
SBO declares ownership in Form BEN-1
Company files Form BEN-2 with ROC in 30 days

topics.example: Mr. A holds shares on behalf of Mr. B. Mr. A files MGT-4 and Mr. B files MGT-5 with the company. The company then files MGT-6 with the ROC.
remember: Form MGT-4: Registered owner's declaration.
Form MGT-5: Beneficial owner's declaration.
Form MGT-6: Company's return to ROC.
SBO Threshold under SBO Rules: 10% indirect/combined rights.
mistakes: Thinking that non-filing of declaration under Sec 89 carries no civil impact; in reality, rights regarding the shares become unenforceable in court.

quiz.q: Which form must a company file with the ROC after receiving a declaration of beneficial interest?
quiz.why: Form MGT-6 is the return filed by the company with the Registrar under Section 89(6).

quiz.q: Under the SBO Rules, what is the minimum percentage threshold for indirect/combined holding to qualify as an SBO?
quiz.why: Rule 2(1)(h) specifies a threshold of not less than 10% of shares, voting rights, or distributable dividend.

topics.title: Annual Return and Inspection of Documents
explain: Every company must prepare an Annual Return in Form MGT-7 (MGT-7A for OPC and Small Companies) after the close of the financial year.
The Annual Return must be filed with the ROC within 60 days from the date of the AGM or the date when it should have been held.
Listed companies or companies with paid-up capital of ₹10 crore+ or turnover of ₹50 crore+ must get MGT-7 certified in Form MGT-8 by a practicing CS.
Registers and copies of returns must be kept at the registered office or where over 1/10th members reside if approved by special resolution.
Registers of members are preserved permanently; annual returns and debenture registers are kept for 8 years.

flow.title: Filing and Preservation of Annual Return
steps: Prepare Annual Return post financial year end
Get signing by Director and CS (or MGT-8 certification)
Hold Annual General Meeting
File MGT-7/7A with ROC in 60 days
Preserve return copy for 8 years

topics.example: XYZ Ltd holds its AGM on 20th September. It must file its Annual Return in Form MGT-7 with the ROC within 60 days, i.e., by 19th November.
remember: MGT-7: Standard Annual Return.
MGT-7A: Abridged return for OPC and Small Companies.
Filing period: Within 60 days of AGM.
Certification MGT-8: Paid-up capital ≥ ₹10 Cr OR Turnover ≥ ₹50 Cr.
mistakes: Assuming that if an AGM is cancelled or not held, the 60-day limit does not apply. The limit runs from the date the AGM should have been held.

quiz.q: What is the time limit for filing the Annual Return with the ROC after the AGM is held?
quiz.why: Section 92(4) mandates filing the Annual Return within 60 days from the date of the AGM.

quiz.q: For how long must copies of annual returns and annexed documents be preserved by a company?
quiz.why: Rule 15 requires copies of annual returns and related documents to be preserved for 8 years from filing.

topics.title: Notice of Meeting & Explanatory Statement
explain: A general meeting requires at least 21 clear days' notice in writing or electronically (14 days for Section 8 companies).
'21 clear days' excludes the day of serving the notice and the day of the meeting; add 48 hours if sent by post.
Notice must be sent to every member, legal representative/assignee, auditor, and director of the company.
Shorter notice is valid if consented to by 95% of members entitled to vote at an AGM, or majority in number with 95% paid-up capital/voting power at an EGM.
Special business requires an Explanatory Statement under Section 102 detailing material facts and interest of directors/KMPs.

flow.title: Calculation of Clear Notice Period for Postal Delivery
steps: Date of posting notice
Add 48 hours for deemed delivery
Count 21 clear days excluding meeting date
Hold General Meeting on or after 24th day

topics.example: If a notice is posted on 1st August, delivery is deemed on 3rd August. Counting 21 clear days, the meeting can be held on 25th August at the earliest.
remember: 21 clear days requirement for general meetings.
+48 hours when notice is sent by post.
Ordinary business at AGM: Financials/Reports, Dividend, Director retirement, Auditor appointment.
All business at EGM is Special Business.
mistakes: Counting the date of dispatch or date of meeting while calculating 21 clear days.
Forgetting to add 48 hours for service by post.

quiz.q: How many clear days' notice is statutorily required to call a General Meeting for a standard public company?
quiz.why: Section 101(1) specifies a notice period of at least 21 clear days.

quiz.q: Which of the following is considered 'Ordinary Business' at an Annual General Meeting?
quiz.why: Section 102(2) defines 4 items as ordinary business at AGM, including the declaration of dividend.

topics.title: Quorum, Chairman, and Proxies
explain: Quorum is the minimum number of members personally present required to conduct a meeting.
For Public Companies, Quorum is 5 (members ≤ 1000), 15 (members 1001-5000), or 30 (members > 5000). For Private Companies, Quorum is 2.
If Quorum is absent within 30 minutes, meeting stands adjourned to next week (or cancelled if called by requisitionists).
Members elect a Chairman by show of hands unless Articles specify otherwise.
Any member entitled to attend and vote can appoint a Proxy using Form MGT-11, submitted at least 48 hours prior to the meeting.

flow.title: Handling Absence of Quorum at a General Meeting
steps: Meeting start time arrives
Wait 30 minutes for Quorum
If Quorum absent and called by members: Cancelled
If called by Board: Adjourn to next week
At adjourned meeting: Present members form Quorum

topics.example: A public company with 800 members needs 5 members present in person for Quorum. Proxies cannot be counted toward Quorum.
remember: Public Co Quorum: 5 / 15 / 30 members present in person.
Private Co Quorum: 2 members present in person.
Proxy Form MGT-11 must be deposited 48 hours before meeting.
A proxy cannot speak and can only vote on a poll.
mistakes: Believing a proxy can speak at a general meeting.

quiz.q: What is the Quorum for a public company having 3,500 members as on the date of the meeting?
quiz.why: Section 103 specifies a quorum of 15 members personally present for member count between 1001 and 5000.

quiz.q: By when must a proxy form (Form MGT-11) be deposited with the company before the meeting?
quiz.why: Section 105(4) provides that proxy forms received 48 hours before the meeting are valid.

topics.title: Modes of Voting: Show of Hands, Electronic, Poll, and Postal Ballot
explain: Voting is first done by show of hands (Sec 107) unless e-voting applies or a poll is demanded.
Listed companies and companies with ≥1000 members must provide e-voting facilities (Sec 108, Rule 20).
E-voting must remain open for at least 3 days and close at 5:00 p.m. on the day prior to the AGM.
A Poll (Sec 109) can be demanded by members holding ≥1/10th voting power or paid-up share capital of ₹5 lakh+.
Postal Ballot (Sec 110) allows voting by post/electronic means for specific items like object clause alteration or share buyback.

flow.title: E-Voting Timeline and Process
steps: Send meeting notice with e-voting details
Publish newspaper notice 21 days prior
Open e-voting for minimum 3 days
Close e-voting at 5:00 p.m. day before meeting
Scrutinizer unblocks votes and submits report in 3 days

topics.example: Company X with 2,000 members must provide e-voting. Shareholders can cast votes electronically from home during the 3-day window.
remember: E-voting mandatory: Listed companies or members ≥ 1000.
E-voting window: Minimum 3 days, closes at 5 PM day before meeting.
Poll demand threshold: 1/10th voting power OR ₹5,00,000 paid-up capital.
Scrutinizer report on poll/e-voting: Submit within 7 / 3 days.
mistakes: Thinking a member who voted via remote e-voting cannot attend the physical AGM. They can attend, but cannot vote again.

quiz.q: At what time must remote e-voting close on the date preceding the general meeting?
quiz.why: Rule 20(4)(vi) specifies that remote e-voting shall close at 5.00 p.m. on the day preceding the meeting.

quiz.q: In a company with share capital, what paid-up share capital threshold allows members to demand a poll?
quiz.why: Section 109(1) permits members holding shares of aggregate paid-up value not less than ₹5,00,000 to demand a poll.

topics.title: Circulation of Resolutions & Representations
explain: Members holding at least 1/10th of total voting power can requisition the company to circulate proposed resolutions.
Requisition for a resolution notice must be deposited at least 6 weeks before the meeting.
Requisition for any other statement must be deposited at least 2 weeks before the meeting.
Requisitionists must deposit a reasonable sum to cover expenses incurred by the company.
The President of India, State Governors, and corporate bodies can appoint representatives who enjoy full voting rights as members.

flow.title: Member Requisition for Resolution Circulation
steps: Eligible members (1/10th voting power) sign requisition
Deposit requisition 6 weeks prior to meeting
Deposit funds for company expenses
Company circulates notice and statement to members

topics.example: Shareholders holding 12% voting power want to move a resolution at the upcoming AGM. They must submit the requisition and expense money 6 weeks in advance.
remember: Threshold: 1/10th of paid-up capital/voting power.
Time limit: 6 weeks before meeting for resolution, 2 weeks for statement.
Corporate representatives (Sec 113) can vote in person, by proxy, or postal ballot.
mistakes: Confusing the 6-week limit for resolution circulation with the 21-day standard notice period.

quiz.q: How many weeks prior to a meeting must a member's requisition for circulating a resolution be deposited at the registered office?
quiz.why: Section 111(2)(c) mandates that the requisition requiring notice of a resolution must be deposited at least 6 weeks before the meeting.

quiz.q: What voting rights does a corporate representative appointed under Section 113 enjoy?
o: Can vote only on show of hands
Same rights as an individual member including proxy and postal ballot
Can vote only if approved by Chairman
quiz.why: Section 113 provides that a corporate representative can exercise the same rights and powers as the body corporate itself.

topics.title: Types of Resolutions & Filing Requirements
explain: An Ordinary Resolution is passed when votes cast in favor exceed votes cast against (simple majority > 50%).
A Special Resolution requires votes in favor to be at least 3 times the votes cast against (≥ 75% majority).
Special Notice (Sec 115) is required for removing a director or appointing an auditor other than the retiring auditor.
Special Notice must be sent by members holding ≥1% voting power or ₹5 lakh paid-up capital, 14 days to 3 months before the meeting.
All Special Resolutions and certain Board resolutions must be filed with ROC in Form MGT-14 within 30 days.

flow.title: Special Notice Resolution Process
steps: Eligible members give Special Notice to company
Notice sent 14 days to 3 months before meeting
Company notifies members 7 days before meeting
Resolution put to vote at meeting
If passed, file Form MGT-14 in 30 days

topics.example: To pass a Special Resolution where 10 votes are cast against, at least 30 votes must be cast in favor.
remember: Ordinary Resolution: Simple majority (Votes for > Votes against).
Special Resolution: 3:1 ratio (Votes for ≥ 3 x Votes against).
Special Notice eligibility: 1% voting power OR ₹5,00,000 paid-up capital.
MGT-14 filing time: Within 30 days of passing.
mistakes: Calculating Special Resolution percentage based on total members rather than members entitled and voting.
Abstain votes are ignored in calculating the 3:1 majority ratio.

quiz.q: If 12 votes are cast against a proposed Special Resolution, how many minimum votes in favor are needed to pass it?
quiz.why: Section 114(2) requires votes in favor to be at least 3 times the votes cast against (12 x 3 = 36).

quiz.q: In which e-form must special resolutions be filed with the Registrar of Companies under Section 117?
quiz.why: Rule 24 mandates filing copies of resolutions required under Section 117 in Form MGT-14.

topics.title: Minutes of Proceedings, Inspection & Electronic Records
explain: Minutes of every meeting must be prepared, signed, and kept in bound minute books within 30 days of the meeting.
Minutes of Board meetings are signed by the Chairman of the same or next meeting; General meeting minutes are signed by the Chairman within 30 days.
Minutes must give a fair and correct summary; defamatory, irrelevant, or detrimental matters can be excluded by Chairman's discretion.
Minute books of General Meetings must be kept at the registered office and open for member inspection for at least 2 hours daily.
Companies with ≥1000 security holders or listed companies may maintain records in electronic form under Section 120.

flow.title: Preparation and Signing of Minutes
steps: General Meeting concludes
Draft proceedings and fair summary
Enter in minute book within 30 days
Chairman signs and dates within 30 days
Preserve minute books permanently

topics.example: General meeting minutes must be entered in the minute book and signed by the Chairman within 30 days after the AGM concludes.
remember: Time limit for entering minutes: 30 days.
General meeting minute books: Preserved permanently at registered office.
Member inspection: Free for at least 2 hours on every working day.
Soft copies of minutes of past 3 financial years: Provided free of cost on request.
mistakes: Believing members can inspect Board meeting minutes. Section 119 allows members to inspect General Meeting minutes only.

quiz.q: Within how many days from the conclusion of a general meeting must the minutes be entered into the minute book?
quiz.why: Section 118(1) mandates entering minutes in the books within 30 days of conclusion of the meeting.

quiz.q: For how long must the minute books of general meetings be preserved by a company?
quiz.why: Rule 25 specifies that minute books of general meetings shall be preserved permanently.

topics.title: General Meetings: AGM, EGM & OPC Rules
explain: Every company (except OPC) must hold an AGM each year; gap between two AGMs cannot exceed 15 months.
First AGM must be held within 9 months from close of 1st financial year; subsequent AGMs within 6 months from FY end.
ROC can extend time for holding subsequent AGMs by up to 3 months for special reasons, but cannot extend First AGM.
Board or requisitionists (holding ≥1/10th paid-up capital/voting power) can call an Extra-Ordinary General Meeting (EGM).
Listed public companies must file a Report on AGM in Form MGT-15 within 30 days of AGM.
For One Person Companies (OPC), procedural sections 98 and 100-111 do not apply; entering resolution in minute book suffices.

flow.title: Timeline for Holding Subsequent AGM
steps: Financial year ends on 31st March
Calculate 6 months from FY end (30th Sept)
Check max gap of 15 months from last AGM
Hold AGM on earlier of the two dates
File Report on AGM MGT-15 within 30 days

topics.example: A company closing FY on 31st March 2024 must hold its subsequent AGM by 30th September 2024 unless ROC grants an extension.
remember: First AGM: Within 9 months of FY end (No ROC extension allowed).
Subsequent AGM: Within 6 months of FY end & max 15 months gap.
ROC Extension: Max 3 months (Only for subsequent AGMs).
Form MGT-15: Report on AGM by listed public companies within 30 days.
mistakes: Assuming ROC can grant an extension for holding the First AGM.
Confusing AGM timing rules with EGM rules.

quiz.q: What is the maximum extension period the ROC can grant for holding a subsequent Annual General Meeting?
quiz.why: Section 96(1) provides that ROC can extend the time for subsequent AGMs by a maximum of 3 months.

quiz.q: Which form must be filed by a listed public company as a Report on AGM under Section 121?
quiz.why: Section 121 read with Rule 31 requires listed public companies to file a Report on AGM in Form MGT-15 within 30 days.
